title: Taiwan Announces 3-Day Joint Precision-Strike Live-Fire Drill at Jiupeng Base
detail: Taiwan's military announced a three-day joint precision-munitions live-fire exercise running Wednesday through Friday (Sept. 16-18, 2026) at Jioupeng Base in Pingtung County, with warning zones extending off the southeastern coast from Taitung to Pingtung counties toward Green Island and Orchid Island. The drill, involving the Army, Navy, Air Force and Coast Guard, is designed to test long-range precision-strike capability and joint wartime combat coordination; planned systems include Patriot and Tian Kung (Sky Bow) air-defense missiles, Hsiung Feng (Brave Wind) II/III anti-ship missiles, HIMARS and ALTIUS-600M loitering munitions, with the decommissioned Chi Yang-class frigate Lan Yang serving as a target vessel. The Navy will separately conduct wartime-transition procedures during the exercise. PAC-3 interceptors are expected to be excluded unless separately approved by Washington, given cost and data-sensitivity concerns.

title: China Warns It Could Cancel Sept. 24 Trump-Xi Summit If US Approves New Taiwan Arms Sale
detail: China warned Washington through diplomatic channels that it could cancel the planned September 24, 2026 Trump-Xi summit at the White House if the US approves new arms sales to Taiwan beforehand, according to multiple sources cited by Japan's Kyodo News on September 12-13. Beijing restated that the Taiwan question is 'the first impassable red line' in bilateral relations; Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun separately said China's opposition to Taiwan arms sales is 'consistent, clear-cut and resolute.' The warning centers on a $14 billion arms package Congress authorized in January 2026 that remains under White House review, on top of the record $11 billion package approved in December 2025. Trump has called Taiwan arms sales a potential 'very good bargaining chip' in talks with Xi and is reportedly eager to secure a diplomatic win from the summit ahead of November's midterms, leaving him to choose between approving the sale and risking the summit, or withholding it and drawing criticism over Taiwan's security.

sources.name: Taipei Times — China threatens US meeting over arms sales
Kyiv Post — Beijing Warns US It May Cancel Xi-Trump Summit Over Taiwan Weapons

confidenceReason: Reporting traces to Kyodo News citing unnamed diplomatic sources; no on-record US or PRC government confirmation of a formal cancellation threat, though Guo Jiakun's on-record 'red line' remarks corroborate the underlying position.
